narrative_purpose: Shows why the same wing flies more easily on Pandora: lower gravity and denser air both cut the speed a flier must reach before takeoff - the chapter's payoff, the two dials that slide the flight ceiling upward.
subject: A two-panel takeoff comparison against a dark page. LEFT panel marked as Earth: a flier running a long distance along a ground line before lifting off, with a tall vertical bar beside it standing for the high required-takeoff-speed. RIGHT panel marked as Pandora: the same flier lifting off after a much shorter run, with a noticeably shorter vertical bar beside it. Beneath both panels sit two small simple round gauges: one showing a lower gravity level, one showing a denser, heavier air (drawn as more, thicker air particles), both visually pushing the right-hand bar down.
scene: A dark diagram space, the two panels side by side with a faint ground line in each, deep haze beyond.
camera: A flat side-on view of both panels so the run-length and the height of each speed-bar read at a glance.
light: Cool clinical glow, faint bioluminescent tracing on the flier and the bars, deep indigo shadow.
palette: Void-indigo ground, cool grey fliers and ground lines, teal for the Pandora bar and cyan glow on the gauges, a restrained amber for the taller Earth bar.
style: Painterly naturalist diagram, hand-painted texture, clean comparative clarity.
detail_level: Crisp on the two fliers, the run-lengths, the two speed-bars, and the gauges; background dissolving into haze.
composition: Earth panel left, Pandora panel right, the two speed-bars clearly different heights, the two gauges along the bottom, generous dark margins for callouts, 16:9.
consistency_notes: Cool Pandora palette with one restrained amber accent on the Earth bar. Same dark glowing mood as the chapter's other plates.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no cartoon or anime style
